notes: All model measurements use low_memory_mode=false, full resident P_LL and two recycles.
Before/after replacements were measured in separate serial processes, each paired against native transitions while keeping other acceleration enabled.
Denoiser tables use 5 warmups and 30 synchronized samples; all samples, including host-latency outliers, are retained.
FP32 microbench reports predate the dtype option and used float32 inputs; the additional BF16 report matches the profiled pair-transition input dtype.
Microbench timings exclude RMSNorm, compilation and initial weight preparation; native graph capture disables autocast weight caching while the accelerator retains BF16 weights explicitly.
The isolated synthetic oracle is the repository native transition expression, not the removed kernel.
Profile run is diagnostic only and excluded from timing comparisons.
Full sampling includes preparation, graph capture and first accelerated startup; excludes checkpoint loading and file writing. Order: baseline, accelerated, accelerated, baseline.
Full sampling average is higher than the preceding imported-kernel report (10.82 vs 9.97 seconds); this is not claimed to be a full-sampling speed improvement over that version.
Biological quality and bitwise full-trajectory equivalence are not established.
Local artifacts: local/results/rfd3-independent-transition/. Initial candidate microbenchmarks are exploratory; final measurements are selected explicitly below.
